findings.description: same_contemporaneous_pool is no longer hardcoded: routing_check now derives it from the data flow on the first joint (N rows == joint, P rows == joint with the neighbour block row-permuted and own columns intact, 0 rows == joint with neighbour slots zeroed), so no source can read any other time step or an exogenous bank. Verified empirically: valid design -> True; a stale-time-step/donor-style P (fixed donor matrix) -> False and also fails the per-joint drift gate.
findings.resolution_note: Confirmed fixed in the working tree. Same-pool flag is computed from source_rows outputs on the first joint; the per-joint actual_p_rows_match_declared_row_perm drift gate additionally runs on every joint, so an exogenous read on any joint is caught. py_compile OK; new negative test test_stale_time_step_source_fails_same_pool kills the donor-style mutation.

findings.description: The mandatory redesign spec section 3.3 lists five required negative/mutation classes; the original suite covered only three (aborted i+2 double-copy, true-neighbour, fixed-point). Missing dedicated tests for a single-slot swap and for a cross-time-step/donor-bank read.
findings.resolution_note: Confirmed fixed: test_single_slot_swap_fails_per_slot_pools and test_stale_time_step_source_fails_same_pool added; all five spec mutation classes are now covered and 19/19 tests pass. Verified empirically that the slot-swap mutation is killed (tuple multiset + drift gates fire) and the stale/donor mutation is killed (same_contemporaneous_pool + drift gates fire). Cosmetic nit only: the slot-swap test name says 'fails_per_slot_pools' while its assertions (and my probe) show per-slot pools stay equal for a within-column swap; the mutation is nonetheless genuinely killed by the tuple-multiset and drift gates.

findings.description: The float-equality value-level collapse check could false-FAIL a valid design on degenerate joints; it was conflated with the authoritative source-ID structure proof.
findings.resolution_note: Confirmed fixed: the value-level check is now a separate reported field actual_row_value_collapse_absent, distinct from the authoritative ID-based no_within_tuple_source_collapse; both are required in routing_gate()'s required_flags and in rehearsal's passed conjunction. Verified: valid design -> both True; true-neighbour mutation -> value collapse False while ID structure stays True.

findings.description: The true-neighbour test's assertions now correctly target the realized-slot identity, declared-row-perm drift, and value-collapse gates (realized_slot_identity_ok False, actual_p_rows_match_declared_row_perm False, actual_row_value_collapse_absent False).
findings.resolution_note: Substantively fixed: assertions updated to the realized-slot/drift/value gates and verified to fire on the mutation. Residual cosmetic issue: the function docstring at lines 150-151 still reads 'must fail the non-neighbour structure check', which my probe shows does not fire (no_p_source_is_true_neighbour remains True because the structure proof is ID-based and immune to the source_rows monkeypatch). The stale wording does not affect test correctness or the gate; a one-line docstring edit would fully close it.
